accounting.quantile: p90 of the signed drift (positive = paid MORE than the decision price, the adverse side for a buy)

justification: Measured on 84,556 of our own decisions (candidate_sft_c8 train/validation/examination, 220,561 rows read, 84,919 carrying a decision clock and a following print) matched to the first notional-qualified print (>=1,000,000 lamports, the same tradeable-print floor rl_reward_v3 uses) of the same mint at or after the decision clock in the 15.9M-row canonical/renormalized_v7 trade tape. The honest headline is that the decision price is NOT a biased estimate of the fill: the median drift is -0.5 bp and 49.3% of fills are worse than the decision price, so there is no systematic decision-to-fill penalty and an artifact that charged one would be inventing it. What is real is the DISPERSION: p25/p75 are -413/+376 bp and the adverse p90 is +1,863 bp; capping the population to fills within 30 s of the decision still gives p90 +1,349 bp, so the tail is execution-window dispersion rather than only quiet mints matched to a print hours later. The shipped value is p90 of the SIGNED drift - the adverse side for a buy - because the reward is required to be conservative against the realized return (readiness class E), NOT because the mean is positive. Alternatives and why they were not shipped: the exact mirror of the exit artifact p25 sell penalty would be p75 (+376 bp), too lenient to bound a cost that sits between the decision and the first tick; p99 (+51,822 bp) is dominated by the tape coverage artifact (fill latency p90 151 s, p99 8 h) rather than by a price we would deliberately cross. The venue split is reported and does not hide a worse market: curve p90 +1,772 bp vs AMM p90 +2,175 bp bracket the pooled +1,863 bp, so the pooled value understates the AMM market by 14% and the stress value records the worse venue. Instances whose fill/decision ratio leaves the 1000x band (the unit-error class) are counted and excluded, never winsorized into the quantiles: 354 of 84,910.
